narrative:
Your law school application was denied because the model estimated a 63% probability that you would fail the bar exam on your first attempt. That is a prediction, not a certainty, but it was high enough to drive the rejection. The strongest influence was your third-year class standing: you were in the lowest decile, while accepted students averaged around the sixth decile, and this strongly pushed the prediction toward failure. The second most important factor was your law school admission test score of 22, compared with an accepted-student average of about 37; this also pushed toward failure. Your first-year class standing, third decile versus an accepted average near the sixth, was the third most important factor and modestly pushed toward passing, but it was not enough to offset the other two signals.

Because the denial is tied to predicted bar-exam risk, your next step should be to strengthen the evidence that you can pass. Ask admissions whether feedback or reconsideration is available. If you reapply, retake the admission test if feasible, consider a structured preparation course, and document academic improvement or bar-readiness support. Speak with advisors about programs with strong bar-exam support, and present a concrete plan showing how you will address the weaknesses the model identified.
